items.title: Sebi proposes to expand FPI play in commodities
items.description: In a strategic move, the Securities and Exchange Board of India has unveiled plans to enable foreign investors to trade in commodity derivatives. This initiative is designed to expand engagement within India's commodity derivatives market. International participants will soon be able to trade physically settled non-agricultural contracts, with the requirement to settle positions before the tender period starts.

items.title: Big investors outperform Nifty, bring in double-digit returns
items.description: During Q1 of FY27, marquee investors saw remarkable success, as their stock portfolios delivered returns ranging from 9.7% to a staggering 39.9% between April and June. Ashish Dhawan emerged as the frontrunner, closely followed by other top investors like Ashish Kacholia. Their impressive performance clearly outstripped the Nifty and Nifty 500 market averages, highlighting their substantial stakes in companies with holdings exceeding one thousand crore.

items.title: Stocks in news: L&T, Tata Motors, HAL, Grasim, NBCC and IRCTC
items.description: The Indian equity markets concluded the trading session on a low note, as escalating crude oil prices weighed heavily on worldwide market sentiment. Notable developments included Larsen & Toubro's announcement of a strategic business transfer for its data center services. Focus will also be on firms like Tata Motors and Hindustan Aeronautics.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks concluded lower on Tuesday, August 11, with Nifty 50 falling below 24,500. Crude oil price rebound and F&O expiry volatility impacted investor sentiment significantly. Market momentum now shifts towards the upcoming U.S. Consumer Price Index data release. Foreign portfolio investors net bought shares worth Rs 258.55 crore on Tuesday. The Indian rupee traded weaker, declining around 15 paise to 95.43.

items.title: Manappuram ends family-led era as Bain brings in a professional MD
items.description: Manappuram Finance will shift to professional management after Bain Capital gained joint control, with VP Nandakumar becoming non-executive chairman and Ashish Singh taking over as MD and CEO from January 2027. First-quarter profit jumped over four-fold to ₹585 crore.

items.title: Stocks to buy in 2026 for long term: Gland Pharma, Star Cement among 5 stocks that could give 10-30% return
items.description: Brokerages remain bullish on a host of stocks, with Star Cement, Poonawalla Fincorp, Hexaware Technologies and Godrej Consumer Products receiving Buy ratings.We have collated a list of recommendations from top brokerage firms from ETNow and other sources:

items.title: Buy, Sell or Hold: Citi recommends buy on Godrej Consumer Products; Goldman Sachs maintains buy on Astra Microwave
items.description: Brokerages remain bullish on Astra Microwave, Kalpataru Projects International and Godrej Consumer Products, citing strong growth prospects, improving financials and stable business strategies. Goldman Sachs raised Astra Microwave’s target on robust margins and order inflows, while Nuvama upgraded Kalpataru Projects after a strong Q1FY27 and better balance sheet.

items.title: MCX shares rise 2% as JPMorgan upgrades, raises target price after this Sebi proposal
items.description: Shares of Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) rose more than 2% after Sebi proposed widening foreign portfolio investors’ access to physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives. JPMorgan upgraded MCX to ‘Overweight ’, and Jefferies retained a ‘Buy’ rating, citing the potential for higher trading volumes and earnings.

items.title: Lenskart, Delhivery, among 10 stocks with highest increase in DII holdings in Q1. See full list
items.description: Domestic institutional investors stepped up buying in several stocks during the June quarter, with DII holdings rising sharply across a number of companies. The increase in ownership came alongside varied stock price performances, highlighting the stocks where domestic institutions raised their exposure the most during the quarter. Here’s the full list.

items.title: Senco Gold shares fall over 8% after Q1 results. What squeezed profitability?
items.description: Senco Gold shares fell 8.16% after the company reported mixed Q1 FY27 results. While consolidated revenue surged 67% YoY to Rs 3,056 crore, PAT declined 3% to Rs 101 crore. EBITDA rose 16% to Rs 213 crore, but margins contracted sharply amid promotional discounting, lower gold prices and customs duty changes, weighing on profitability and investor sentiment.

items.title: 44 bullish & bearish stock picks across sectors for August by Axis Direct
items.description: A sector-wise technical outlook points to a broadly positive market trend, with banking, capital goods, realty, consumer durables, healthcare, power and auto sectors showing bullish setups. The brokerage recommends a buy-on-dips strategy across several sectors, while selective caution is advised in FMCG, metals and oil & gas despite their broader technical resilience.

items.title: Manappuram Finance shares jump 3% after Q1 profit soars 4x. Why Jefferies, Morgan Stanley raised target prices
items.description: Manappuram Finance shares witnessed an uptick on Wednesday after Q1 FY27 profit surged nearly four-fold to Rs 585 crore. Jefferies raised its target price to Rs 430, citing better NII and lower provisions, while Morgan Stanley also raised its target. CLSA retained a Hold rating, with a Rs 350 target price.

items.title: FMCG’s FII nightmare! $5.2 billion selloff in 12 straight months. Are stocks set for a rebound?
items.description: Over the past year, foreign investors have unloaded $5.2 billion worth of FMCG stocks, largely due to the challenges stemming from inflated valuations and rising input costs. Companies are now transferring these increased costs to customers, resulting in weak volume growth and declining margins. For a recovery to take shape, analysts emphasize the need for enhanced consumer spending and stable commodity prices.

items.title: Zydus Lifesciences shares drop 3% after Q1 earnings. Here's why Nuvama upgraded rating, hiked target
items.description: Shares of Zydus Lifesciences saw a decline of more than two percent following the announcement of a notable profit drop. The net profit plunged thirty-six percent year-on-year for the first quarter, despite a nearly twenty-two percent increase in operational revenue. Expenses surged by over forty-one percent. However, the managing director remains optimistic about future prospects. Analysts at Nuvama have upgraded the stock to 'Buy', setting a higher price target.

items.title: Missed these IPOs after cold debuts? 11 stocks have since soared up to 222% in few months
items.description: Despite underwhelming debuts for eleven IPOs, the market has witnessed a remarkable recovery in their valuations. Stocks have soared impressively, with gains ranging from 23% to a staggering 222% over their initial offer prices. Notably, Omnitech Engineering rebounded dramatically, rising by 222% after an initial drop of 9.63%. This underscores the fact that performance on listing day may not accurately predict long-term success.

items.title: Sensex falls over 200 points, Nifty below 24,450 as oil nears $90/barrel. What lies ahead?
items.description: On Wednesday, Indian stocks experienced a downturn as oil prices approached $90 per barrel.  Analysts attribute this decline to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which are hampering market momentum. Despite this, the resilience of India's growth suggests improved corporate earnings for FY27, while mid and small-cap stocks have been highly active due to recent results.

items.title: Godrej Consumer Products shares tank 10% after CEO’s sudden exit; HSBC downgrades to Hold
items.description: Godrej Consumer Products shares declined 10% following the sudden resignation of CEO Sudhir Sitapati, who announced his work was finished and it was time for new beginnings. HSBC nalysts have since downgraded the stock, highlighting potential uncertainties and execution hurdles ahead, despite the company showcasing strong Q1 performance with impressive profit and revenue growth. Aasif Malbari is set to take charge as the new CEO.
